title: Retd. Gen. Zameer Uddin Shah on how the army waited for 24 hrs in an airfield while Gujarat burned
description: In conversation with ThePrint, ex-AMU VC and Retd. Gen. Zameer Uddin Shah talks about the 2002 Gujarat riots and how he had to go there to curb the increasing tensions between Hindu and Muslims in a communal clash. He adds that there was a complete mayhem in the state and the police were ineffective and picked the side of the majority groups. He met then CM Narendra Modi and then defence minister George Fernandes to figure out a way to control the situation but there was not much they could do. asr.full_text: Press the bell icon on YouTube and don't miss another update. You were asked to go to, from Jodhpur? When the riots broke out in Gujarat, you were asked to go to Gujarat immediately? The riots broke out on 27th of February after the dead bodies were brought. I think it was a blunder to have brought them in a convoy but that was an administrative decision. But anyway, it inflamed passions. People who saw the trucks and the bodies, obviously, their passion got inflamed. It shouldnít have been done. AnywayÖ So, you reached when did you when do you reach Ahmedabad? I reached, see let me give you the whole chronology, on 27th evening when I was, I had just attended an exercise, I got a call from General Padmanabhan, then chief, I was a little surprise because generally we follow the chain of command. It should have been to the command headquarters, to the core headquarters and then to me, to the divisional commander. Right. But he says Zoom, that's my army name, I'm are called Zum. I am called Zum. Why you are you called Zum if I may ask. Well I was in relative in school. Okay. So, everybody has a name. So, general Padmanabhan said to you. Zum get moving, get your troops into Ahmedabad, and he says cut out the riots. So, I said, sir, it will take me 48 hours to reach, he says don't worry the Air Force is laying on the aircraft, so I said right sir, I sent a message to my deputy JOC, my Brigadier, I said get the troops moving, we were already mobilised and I got into my gypsy along with my ADC and I reached the airfield at about 10 pm Ok. This is on the night of the 27th? on the night of the 28th of Feb? The night of 28th Feb I reached the airfield. And in the but if you can tell the story, No, in Jodhpur. The aircraft was coming in. Air force aircraft. And I didn't wait. I took the first aircraft with the troops who had come and I flew into Ahmedabad. The rest of the troops, about 3000 of them, came onto the airfield, and 60 flights brought us in. Total 12 companies, no 6 but 24 companies of the infantry 6, but at 24 companies. Okay. Of the infantry, flown in on that night. So, when do you reach Ahmedabad? Do you reach on the… I reached at about a midnight of first, second. First, or 28th, first. I reached at midnight. So, the depute Jocy of the formation or Brig. Mera met me And what did you do? once you reached Ahmedabad your book said that you reached at round 1 or 2 a.m. and what happened? So, I was expecting the transport the magistrate the police guide and the communications to be there, I found nothing except for Brigadier. So I said where is all the logistics we had been promised? Well he said the state government will arrange that I've got nothing to do with it. So, I said, where's the Chief Secretary? He says, he's abroad. Who's officiating? He gave me some numbers. I tried to call, call, call, there was no reply. So, I thought the best way to handle it is to go and report to the Chief minister. Then chief minister Mr. Narendra Modi. A guide was there. And I reached his house at 2 a.m. on the first of March. We traversed through horrendous sites. We were supposed to be informed. Police there with lathis. They had not any weapons. The mobs did rampage and pillage. What was the police doing? Nothing, they were just standing there. Ma'am, they didn't touch us but I told the Chief Minister and that there is a terrible mayhem going on. You told the Chief Minister! He always knew it. I said, we had been promised these things they are not there. And I said where the trouble spot is. I had taken the tourist map. I didn't have a map of the city. So, we plotted out. So, who else was there? Yourself? Yes. Fortunately there the Raksha Minister was looking very worried. and he was already there at that location. Who else was there? Yourself? fortunately the Raksha Mantri was there. Mr George Fernandes looking worried. He was already there they were eating late dinner at 2 AM. So I joined in and then we decided so yourself George Fernandes and then Chief Minister Narendra Modi all three of us decided on the deployment of the army and I requested Immediately I said we need the transport. We need magistrates police gauge communicator, and he agreed he said. Yes, they'll come So I headed back I the troops landed and We kept waiting nothing came. So then what happened then so we were at the field and that morning then Mr George Fernandez came and addressed the troops at about 10 o'clock You but you stayed on we stayed on there feel I mean vague see in a city where you gone foot And that morning, then Mr. George Fernandez came in addressed the troops and about, a 10 or 11. You. But you stayed there? We stayed on the airfield. See, in the city where to go on foot we don't know. So, no orders were given to the Indian army, to yourself, and to your troops. No, I was given orders. No, but to come into the city and to… I didn't have the wherewithal. I was given clear orders curb the violence. Where where do I go without transport, without you know, So, whose responsibilities is this, to have given you the where with all? Well, it was the state government, I think it was failure of, the chief secretary was not there, so I don't know who the chief minister gave orders to. It was a case of administrative failure total. So, who do you think should take responsibility? I will not make a statement, I will not make a statement on that. The Chief Minister himself would know who is responsible but it was a case of administrative failure. The Home Minister perhaps? The Home Minister of the State? Whoever it was I don't comment on politicians or politics. I only deal with administrators. But since the chief executive is not there I have to go to the chief minister directly. We found out, I deployed three battalions in Ahmedabad. How long did it take for the orders to come? How long did it take for you to get into the city? The transport came, the transport came on second at 10'o clock. So, for a whole 24 or more than 24 hours. We were sitting at the airport, that's right. Not doing very much. So, then on the second you come out in to the city and what do you see? I found mayhem, I found, so, we, we opened fire at the asanas and I think we killed two or three and wounded about 20 are given stick taught us that firing most we blow the belt and that's why the casualty two less some casuities were carried away by by workers of the right-wing what you mean there were people there were people who were short but they were carried away. We couldn't recover their bodies. You couldn't travel they were carried away to maybe to a hospital or wherever they were and there I found that surrounded minority pockets with crowds being for the blood and the police firing into the windows of the buildings. So I said, what are you doing? They said, we're keeping the mob at bay. I said then fire the other way. you doing? They are not the mobs. So, I said fire. The mobs are Hindu mobs. Majority. I never used religion. It was majority. majority community surrounding the minorities. You have walled ghettos in Ahmedabad. Do you remember names of these places like Juwapura. I forget the names in the whole lot, but police was totally biased and parochial and they were letting flag there, from Muslims through the windows. The poor fellows were trying to protect their building and they are firing through the windows. So, I got very, very angry and but wherever the majority of mobs had to be dealt with, they never took action. It was left to the Army. Or, wherever the mobs of the majority of communities? No, not the majority of the majority of communities! The minorities were all stuck, scared to death in their buildings. So, you are saying, the police took no action? None at all. And, why do you think that? No, I don their buildings. So, you are saying the police took no action? None at all. And why do you think that? No, I don't know. Yes, I am aware that police forces all over the country have got totally communalised. I have seen it in my hometown in Meerut and Sardana. Totally communalised, totally parochial and unreliable. They cannot be trusted in the riot to, because they take sides. So, that was, it explain it's a phenomenon all over the country. You don't think this is true of the Indian army? Oh, not at all. Otherwise we wouldn't have been able to settle the thing within 48 hours. We had curbed violence after they found that we mean business and there is a danger of long term deployment of the armed forces of them getting, well this thing rubbing off on them. And so that's why… So we will talk about that like for example the Armed Forces, Special Powers act in Kashmir as well as in the North East. But to finish the Gujarat story. So you settled, you quelled the riots in 48 hours. They were quelled So you come out into the city on the first of March and by No, the second of March. On the second of March, that's right, because from the second of March and by fourth everything all violent. Of course there's enmity and and ab abusing but no violence. So your experience was of the Gujarat police openly communal, taking sides in favor of the Hindus and against the Muslims. Absolutely, now this is not only a phenomenon in Gujarat . And Did you report this to… Of course. It is… well of course I didn't tell him that a police communal but when the defense minister asked me I said change the police chief sack him. This is to George... I said change him. So he says you have taken the words out of my mouth. These were his words but nothing happened. They didn't change him he was there right through. yes, several months later Mr. Gill. Sita Ghoshri KPS Gill. KPS Gill who was given credit for Punjab and Gujarat. Well, he just came in after the army had done its work.
